items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (encodeShape, maxEncodedCells, totalVertices) and the code follows package style. But the long encodeShape/decode switch blocks have few comments, and short names like `sh` and `n` are used in shape logic.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: About 580 lines were added to shapeindex.go instead of a dedicated shapeindex_encode.go. Shape encoding is inlined in one large encodeShape switch, not placed as methods next to each type. The vertex write loops are copy-pasted for PointVector, LaxPolyline and LaxLoop, and decode looks longer than 100 lines.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length is bounded before allocation, errors are checked at each step, and IDs, cells and edges are validated. Fuzz and truncation tests are included. Magic constants remain: `maxEdgesPerCell > 10000`, `min(nvertices, 4096)`, `min(nloops, 1024)`, `maxEdges = 10`.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Encode/Decode are added methods, the Shape interface is unchanged, and the new tags 6/7/8 sit below typeTagMinUser. Existing behaviour still changed incidentally: LaxLoop/PointVector ChainEdge, LaxPolygon ChainPosition, the Polyline.decode signature, and decodeFaceRun now rejects counts above maxEncodedVertices. Wire formats are the same.
